title: tsdk: schema-driven output typing + runtime validators for streamed & retried responses
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Teams using the TypeScript SDK (tsdk) want a single, ergonomic way to declare structured outputs for LLM responses that yields: (1) strong compile-time types, (2) runtime validation for safety in production, (3) JSON Schema artifacts for external tooling, and (4) good ergonomics for streaming responses and automatic retries. Current ad-hoc patterns (manual type assertions + separate validators) are error-prone and make streaming partial-parses awkward.

Proposal: Implement a schema-driven generation flow in tsdk that: (A) accepts a canonical developer schema (Zod or an equivalent TS-first DSL) as the source of truth; (B) emits TypeScript types, Zod runtime validators, and JSON Schema artifacts during build/typegen; (C) uses a small runtime adapter that: performs incremental validation on streamed chunks, supports discriminated-union parsing via a required discriminator key (configurable, default `__kind`), and guarantees deterministic behavior across retries.

Key components: 
- Developer API: accept `schema` parameter in `client.generate` / `client.chat` calls (overload) and in the TSDK helper `defineOutput(schema)`. Example: `const Out = defineOutput(z.object({ __kind: z.literal('order'), id: z.string(), total: z.number() }));`
- Typegen: augment the generated Promise/AsyncIterator types so `response.output` is strongly typed to the inferred TS type from the schema. Emit JSON Schema to `dist/schemas/<model>-<route>.json` for usage by downstream validators (and console).
- Runtime: small validator wrapper around Zod that supports `validatePartial` for partial stream delta application. Provide `streamingParse` helper which buffers until discrimination is resolvable and yields validated subtrees.
- Discriminated unions: require a discriminator key (configurable). For union types, prefer a `z.discriminatedUnion('__kind', [...])` pattern. Provide backward-compatible fallback for consumers who do not supply a discriminator by attempting heuristics (last-resort, opt-in).
- Retries: when a request is retried due to network/fallback, the runtime must be able to continue parsing deterministically: partial buffers are tied to request-id scope; on retry we attempt to rehydrate the same schema-based parser so validation and fuzzy merging rules are identical.

Acceptance criteria: 
1) `defineOutput` API exists and is typed. 
2) Typegen pipeline emits TS type + JSON Schema + Zod runtime factory. 
3) Runtime streaming parser handles chunked JSON and discriminated unions with minimal developer boilerplate. 
4) Unit tests covering streaming + retry scenarios (include simulated truncated chunks, replays). 
5) Docs + example repo demonstrating product usage and migration guide for existing tsdk consumers.

Compatibility & trade-offs: 
- We will default to Zod for developer ergonomics and reuse existing tsdk Zod helpers; however, we’ll emit JSON Schema so non-Zod consumers can still use the artifact. 
- Requiring a discriminator is the simplest, most robust approach for union types. To ease adoption we will document patterns and add a small ad-hoc heuristic fallback (opt-in). 
- Streaming validation adds runtime overhead; we'll provide a no-op fast-path for consumers who opt out of validation for extreme latency-sensitive flows.

Implementation plan (high-level): 
1) Prototype `defineOutput` and runtime `validatePartial` helpers (2 wk spike).
2) Extend typegen to emit JSON Schema and TS type aliases (3 wk).
3) Implement streamingParse and retry-scope rehydration (2 wk).
4) Integrate into SDK codepaths and add feature flags (1 wk).
5) Tests, perf benchmarks, docs, example app (2 wk).

Example usage (developer ergonomics): 
const Out = defineOutput(z.union([
  z.object({ __kind: z.literal('success'), data: z.object({ id: z.string() }) }),
  z.object({ __kind: z.literal('error'), message: z.string() })
]));

const stream = client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood/small', prompt, outputSchema: Out });
for await (const piece of stream) {
  // piece.type is narrowed by the schema, validated at runtime
  if (piece.output.__kind === 'success') {
    // TypeScript knows piece.output.data.id is string
  }
}

Notes on docs and examples: produce a migration doc that shows common patterns (single object, discriminated unions, arrays), and a streaming example that demonstrates how to safely render partial results while waiting for discriminator to appear.
comments: 2025-02-11: Spike started — prototyped defineOutput + small Zod helper to infer type. Found that zod's .safeParseSync is not incremental; implemented a small incremental JSON buffer + partialParse that feeds full objects to Zod when complete.

2025-02-13: Design review with PM and DX. PM (Lina Zhou) requested JSON Schema artifacts for Console validation and for customers integrating with non-TS stacks. Agreed to emit JSON Schema during typegen.

2025-02-14: Eng review: discussed deterministic behavior for retries. Decided to scope partial buffers to request IDs; on retries we re-initialize buffer and replay any client-side cached deltas (if present). Added an edge-case for the model sending broken discriminators; flagged for monitoring and alerting.
2025-02-16: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tsdk/pull/3142 — contains defineOutput API and basic streamingParse tests. Requesting review from @marco and @diana.
2025-02-17: Perf note: streaming validation adds ~0.8ms per chunk on Node 18 in microbenchmarks with zod. Adding a fast-path (validate: false) opt-out for critical hot paths.
2025-02-18: UX feedback from design (Priya Rao): prefer `__kind` as default discriminator but allow `kind` alias. Will include examples and lint rules in migration guide.
